summary: Wrote a six-phase, record-only plan for the residue-index modulus convention. The convention is recorded by naming the modulus (P + 1 is the modulus; an instantiation names m with 1 <= m and sets P := m - 1, so an exhibited period p enters as m := p) rather than by picking between the two off-by-one readings, with convention-independence grounded on object_only_parameters_refuted and reach_period_refuted. Every probe theorem statement stays byte-for-byte unchanged. Plan-time grep widened the scope beyond the research report: the understated 'dominate' clause occurs at 12 sites across 7 files, including the self-declared-authoritative docs/theorem-index.md, so the sharpening is folded into each file-owning phase with a residual-occurrence grep as the final mechanical check.
